skill.name: orchestration
skill.description: Guides supervised multi-agent coordination in Orca, including task dispatch, messaging, decision gates, worker completion, and safe handoff boundaries.
skill.summary: Coordinate supervised Orca agent work with tasks, dispatches, messages, gates, and worker completion rules.
skill.author: stablyai

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and documented Orca CLI examples in SKILL.md. I found no prompt injection attempt, malware intent, data exfiltration behavior, or hidden executable code in the reviewed skill file.

remediation.issue: Markdown command examples trigger static external-command detections.
remediation.suggestion: Keep command examples explicit, scoped to Orca, and paired with clear user-authorization language for destructive or state-reset operations.

remediation.issue: Prompt placeholders may contain user-supplied text when agents copy examples into a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Document that task briefs and prompts must be passed with safe argument handling and proper shell quoting.

content.value_statement: Multi-agent coding tasks can lose ownership, status, and completion signals. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Orca orchestration commands for supervised dispatch, gates, and worker completion.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use Orca orchestration instead of a full handoff.
Provides Orca CLI flows for task creation, dispatch, messaging, gates, and checks.
Defines worker_done, heartbeat, ask, escalation, and decision gate behavior.
Guides supervised task DAGs, rolling waits, and coordinator loops.
Covers worker terminal and worktree selection rules.
Describes recovery limits for resetting runtime orchestration state.
limitations: Requires a running Orca runtime with orchestration enabled.
Requires the Orca CLI to be available in the working environment.
Does not execute orchestration automatically; the agent must run approved commands.
Does not replace human review for destructive commands or broad worker prompts.

use_cases.title: Supervise Parallel Coding Tasks
use_cases.description: Create tracked tasks, dispatch workers, wait for worker_done messages, and summarize results without losing ownership.

use_cases.title: Run Decision-Gated Workflows
use_cases.description: Use gates when a coordinator or user decision must happen before downstream tasks continue.

use_cases.title: Separate Handoffs From Supervision
use_cases.description: Choose full handoff flows when another agent owns the work, and orchestration only when active supervision is required.

prompt_templates.title: Start One Supervised Worker
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Orca orchestration to create one worker for this task: [task]. Wait for worker_done and summarize the result.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Review And Fixes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Orca orchestration to dispatch a review worker and a fix worker. Ask me before any scope changes.

prompt_templates.title: Manage A Decision Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Orca orchestration for this multi-step plan. Create a decision gate before merging outputs or assigning follow-up work.

prompt_templates.title: Run A Parallel DAG
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Orca orchestration to decompose this project into dependent tasks. Dispatch ready tasks in waves, handle escalations, and report final results.

output_examples.input: Use Orca orchestration to have a worker review a branch and report findings.
output_examples.output: The coordinator creates a tracked review task, dispatches a worker, waits for completion, and summarizes confirmed findings and open questions.

output_examples.input: Coordinate two workers, then ask before applying risky fixes.
output_examples.output: The workflow separates review and fix ownership, collects worker results, opens a decision gate, and waits for approval before continuing.

output_examples.input: Hand this project to another agent without supervision.
output_examples.output: The skill directs the agent to use a full handoff path and stop monitoring after prompt delivery.

best_practices: Use orchestration only when the user wants supervision, monitoring, results, gates, or a task DAG.
Verify task and dispatch state before claiming work was orchestrated.
Keep worker ownership clear, especially when review results require follow-up fixes.
anti_patterns: Using orchestration for a full ownership handoff without user supervision requirements.
Monitoring a handoff worker after prompt delivery when the user did not ask for supervision.
Sending dispatch lifecycle messages to groups instead of the concrete coordinator handle.

faq.question: What does this skill coordinate?
faq.answer: It coordinates Orca tasks, dispatches, messages, worker completion, gates, and supervised multi-agent workflows.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when you need active supervision, worker completion tracking, decision gates, or a task DAG.

faq.question: When should I avoid it?
faq.answer: Avoid it for full handoffs where another agent owns the work and no monitoring is requested.

faq.question: Does it require Orca?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires a running Orca runtime, the Orca CLI, and the orchestration feature.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is documented for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows inside Orca.

faq.question: Can it run commands by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides orchestration guidance. The agent still runs commands according to user intent and environment policy.
